main_body: Tall dark stone throne with a high arched backrest, a red cushion seat with a gold trim edge, and a stepped plinth base. The view is straight from the front.
top_band: The seat shows red rows 18-19 (#c30014), then pink rows 20-21 grading to a gold edge at row 22. The pink is the cushion's front face, so only about 2 rows could be a top. The rest of the column is the dark backrest (rows 5-17) and dark body (rows 23-27), with no light horizontal surface.
evidence: The seat surface is not readable from above. The red cushion is a 5-row gradient that reads as a face-on front. Its top is at most a 2-row band, as thin as the 'thin seat' in the guide. The backrest, body and plinth are flat vertical faces in near-black tones, with no visible top surface. The gold row at 22 is only a trim line. This is a front elevation with a thin seat band, so it fails.

style.evidence: Measured facts: 96% of dark edge pixels are neutral, against 1% and 33% for the references, so the outline is a near-black sticker line. The stone body is a stack of almost colourless very dark greys (#131317, #1e1e24, #2a2a32, #41414c), so the forms separate only by a black-ish outline and not by tinted material tones. The candidate has 18 distinct colours against 38-40 for the references, though its colours per tile (16) are close to the references' 17 and 20. The red cushion has a decent ramp and there are no flat fills. The neutral near-black outline and the low overall colour count make it look thinner and more sticker-like than the references.
